doc: The one capability manifest (owner, 2026-10-20): every capability DS offers and how each platform serves it.
A row is keyed by its capability id. A DS Core command's id is its command id (`ds pm task create` is
`pm.task.create`); a capability Core does not carry uses the same dotted form and must not be supported on cli.
Each row names every platform, in platform order, with one value:
core                    supported: installed DS Core, through the host's Core door;
kernel:<module>         supported: the in-page Kernel: src/gateway_exchange/<module>.rs or src/<module>.rs;
network_unit            supported: the governed Network WASM unit in the page;
pending:<reason>        planned here, refused until it lands, with that reason's message;
discarded:<reason>      not offered here, refused with that reason's message.
A platform lists the executors it has; a platform with none takes only pending or discarded.
`export` names a row's one typed owner in the page: the wasm-bindgen JS name the page calls. Every row with a
kernel or network_unit cell names one, and the build refuses an export no Kernel source defines. An export that
serves several rows admits each request by its row (capabilities::admit_export). Where a platform runs a row on
core beside the page (the Desktop), the page may also run it in-page through the same owner.
Optional `run` is how the page calls a Core capability through capabilityRun: the command with the caller's
document as its `input` (inside `wrap`), its fixed `switches`, the `answer` member of its data it reads or the
`output` file it writes, and `page_lanes`, how many jobs a page sends to Core at once.
build.rs (build_capabilities.rs) compiles this file into the Kernel's constant tables and refuses a malformed,
incomplete or non-canonical file. A Kernel build serves the one platform whose `feature` it enables (none: the
`default`). ds-cli's capability_manifest test holds the rows supported on cli to Core's command registry, so a
new Core command cannot ship without a decision for every platform.
To add a platform: add it to `platforms` and run `DS_CAPABILITIES_REWRITE=1 cargo check`, which gives every
row `pending:<platform>_not_yet_supported`; then decide rows, and add a `feature` and one host adapter when
the platform gets a Kernel build. The same command rewrites this file canonically after a hand edit.

platforms.doc: Headless DS Core: the ds CLI, its MCP projection and headless servers.
DS GridDesign Desktop on Linux and Windows: the page with installed DS Core.
The browser page: the in-page Kernel and governed WASM units, without Core.
A future Android app: no adapter or Kernel build yet.
iOS: no adapter or Kernel build.
A future macOS Desktop and Core host: no adapter or Kernel build yet.

reasons.browser_redirect_only: Google sign-in is a browser redirect; DS GridDesign Desktop signs in through its own account flow.
reasons.cli_pipeline_only: Elevation work runs through `ds` and its MCP tools, not in the page.
reasons.drives_desktop_window: This drives the paired DS GridDesign Desktop window from `ds`; the page offers it in its own view.
reasons.engineering_on_core: Engineering processing runs on DS Core for now: open this project in DS GridDesign Desktop, or use `ds`.
reasons.google_redirect_not_registered: Google sign-in waits for its registered sign-in redirect; sign in with email and password meanwhile.
reasons.macos_not_yet_supported: DS GridDesign does not run on macOS yet.
reasons.mobile_not_offered: Not offered on phones: use the Web, DS GridDesign Desktop or `ds`.
reasons.native_host_only: This runs where DS Core is installed: DS GridDesign Desktop or `ds`.
reasons.native_local_layers: Machine-local layers, overlays and live folders are native only: use DS GridDesign Desktop or `ds`.
reasons.network_unit_desktop_pending: Waits for the Network unit loader on DS GridDesign Desktop.
reasons.page_engine_session: An engine session inside the page; `ds` works on DS Grid models with its own `dsgrid` commands.
reasons.page_session: The page's own sign-in; `ds` signs in with `ds auth login` or `ds account connect`.
reasons.printing_on_core: Printing runs on DS Core: use DS GridDesign Desktop or `ds report`.
reasons.solar_web_parity: Solar preparation, runs and publication stay on DS GridDesign Desktop or `ds solar`; the Web calculates a Core-prepared city in its Solar unit.
reasons.store_status_via_core_store: Core reports this record through `ds core store` (store `store_status`, action `status`); a dedicated `ds store status` command has not landed.
reasons.survey_admin_on_core: Survey administration runs on DS Core: use DS GridDesign Desktop or `ds survey`.
reasons.survey_capture_web_android: Survey capture lives on Web and Android.
reasons.terminal_only: A terminal command of `ds` itself; DS GridDesign Desktop and the Web have their own.
reasons.web_download_page: The download page is for browsers; DS GridDesign Desktop updates itself.
reasons.web_parity_pending: Not on the Web yet: use DS GridDesign Desktop or `ds`.
